mekki-muskil:44-44.t: His saying (فذرني ومن يكذب): (من) is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by conjunction with the pronoun of the speaker; or, if you wish, as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment).

mekki-muskil:49-49.t:
His saying (لولا أن تداركه): (أن) is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted; according to Sībawayh it is hardly ever used with (لولا) except omitted. The implied meaning is: "Were it not for Allah's overtaking him, it would have caught him" or "rescued him", or the like. (لنبذ) is the answer (jawāb) of (لولا). (تداركه) is masculine because (النعمة) and (النعم) have one meaning, so it is construed according to the meaning. It is also said that it is masculine because a separation stands between them, namely the hāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. the object pronoun of تداركه separates the verb from its agent]. It is also said: because the femininity of (النعمة) is not real, since it has no masculine from its own word. In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: (لولا أن تداركته), with tāʾ, treating the word as feminine.
His saying (وهو مذموم): a mubtadaʾ and khabar, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative pronoun in (نبذ).

mekki-muskil:51-51.t: His saying (وإن يكاد الذين كفروا ليزلقونك): according to the Kufans, (إن) means (ما) and the lām means (إلا); the implied form is: "And those who disbelieve almost do nothing but make you slip". According to the Basrans, (إن) is lightened from the heavy (إنّ), its noun is implied with it, and the lām is the lām of emphasis, which is obligatory in this kind so that it does not resemble the (إن) that means (ما). Its like has already been discussed.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He, نون والقلم: the justification of pronouncing the nūn clearly (iẓhār) and of assimilating it (idghām) has preceded in [Sūrat] Yā Sīn and elsewhere. It has been read with a fatḥa on the nūn, on the basis that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "mention Nūn" or "recite Nūn"; it is a diptote because it is definite and the name of something feminine, namely the sūra; it is also said: because it is a foreign noun. Sībawayh said the nūn was given a fatḥa only because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, like أين and كيف, as if the reader connected his recitation and did not assimilate, so two quiescent letters came together, the nūn and the wāw, and the nūn was given a fatḥa. Al-Farrāʾ said it was given a fatḥa only by likening it to ثمّ. Others said it was given a fatḥa because it resembled the nūn of the plural. Abū Ḥātim said: when the wāw of the oath was omitted from it, it was made accusative by the verb of swearing, as you say اللهَ لأفعلن ("By Allah, I will surely do it"), making the noun accusative by the verb, as if in the representation [it were "I swear by Allah"], even though أقسم الله is not used. Sībawayh permitted اللهِ لأفعلن in the genitive, making the particle of the oath govern although it is omitted; that was permissible in this, though not permissible elsewhere, because of the frequent use of omission in the chapter of the oath. Whoever makes نون an oath makes the answer [to it] ما أنت بنعمة ربك.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying أَن كَانَ ذَا مَال: أن is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and the governing word in it is an implied verb, its implied form being "he disbelieves" or "he denies, because he has wealth". It is not permissible for the governing word to be تتلى nor قال, because what comes after إذا does not govern what precedes it, since إذا is annexed to the clauses after it, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern what precedes the muḍāf; and قال is the apodosis of the conditional, and it does not govern what precedes the conditional, because the rule of the governor is to come before what it governs, and the rule of the apodosis is to come after the condition, so it would become fronted and postponed at the same time, and that is not permissible. So a governing word must be implied, because of what we mentioned.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t:
His saying مصبحين: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nominative latent pronoun in ليصرمنها; أصبح has no khabar (predicate) in this, because it means "entering upon the morning".
His saying بأيكم الْمفْتُون: the بـ [is redundant], and the meaning is "which of you is the afflicted one" (أيكم المفتون). [Translator's note: a word appears to have dropped after «الباء» in the edition; the following clause («It is also said that the بـ is not redundant») shows that «زائدة» ("redundant") is meant.] It is also said that the بـ is not redundant, but it has the meaning of في; and it is also said that المفتون means الفتون (affliction), the implied form being "in which of you is the affliction", i.e. madness.
أيكم was written in the Muṣḥaf in this place specifically with two yāʾs and an alif before them. The reason for that is that they wrote the hamza with a form according to its full pronunciation (taḥqīq) and a form according to its lightening (takhfīf): the alif is the form of the hamza according to full pronunciation, and the first yāʾ is its form according to lightening, because before the hamza there is a kasra, so when you lighten it, its rule is to be replaced by a yāʾ; and the second yāʾ is the form of the doubled yāʾ. Likewise they wrote بأييد with two yāʾs for this reason; and they wrote ولأاوضعوا with two alifs, and likewise أو لأاذبحنه, ولا إلى الجحيم and لا إلى الله تحشرون — all of it was written with two alifs, one of which, the first, is the form of the hamza according to full pronunciation, and the second its form according to lightening. It has also been said that the first is the form of the hamza and the second the form of its vowel; and it is also said that it is a fatḥa that was prolonged and an alif was generated from it, and there is remoteness in that. This is only a justification of the script of the Muṣḥaf, since it has come that way and there is no way to alter it. This chapter is wide, and it is frequent in the script, departing from the script customary among scribes, so a justification befitting it must be drawn out. We will mention it, if Allah the Exalted wills, exhaustively and with its reasons, in a work other than this. [Translator's note: the edition prints «أذبخنه» and «وَلَا الى الْجَحِيم»; they are rendered here as the intended Muṣḥaf spellings with two alifs.]
His saying قَالَ أساطير الْأَوَّلين: i.e. "these are legends" (هذه أساطير), so أساطير is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject).

mekki-muskil:33-33.t:
His saying كَذَلِك الْعَذَاب: العذاب is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and كذلك the khabar (predicate), i.e. the punishment that befalls the disbelievers is like this punishment.
His saying مَا لكم كَيفَ تحكمون: ما is an interrogative mubtadaʾ, لكم the khabar, and كيف is in the position of the accusative by تحكمون.

mekki-muskil:39-39.t: His saying أم لكم أَيْمَان علينا بالغه: أيمان is a mubtadaʾ (subject), علينا the khabar (predicate), and بالغة a naʿt (adjective) of أيمان. Al-Ḥasan read بالغةً in the accusative, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nominative latent pronoun in علينا.

mekki-muskil:42-42.t: His saying يَوْم يكْشف: يوم is accusative by [an implied] "remember, O Muhammad" (اذكر يا محمد), so you begin with it. It is also possible that يأتوا makes it accusative, i.e. "let them bring their partners on this day"; then beginning with it is not good.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t: His saying خاشعة أَبْصَارهم: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the latent pronoun in يدعون or of the latent pronoun in يستطيعون; أبصارهم is nominative by its verb [i.e. by خاشعة as its agent]. ترهقهم is in the position of a ḥāl like the first; if you wish, it may be detached from the first [i.e. a new sentence].
